function: MA-DRL agents (one per satellite) learn joint satellite and gateway beamformers maximizing weighted sum rate under backhaul constraints, user-centric multi-satellite downlink (pp. 8-10).
system: Two 16-antenna LEO satellites (500 km, Ka band 30 GHz) serve 10 single-antenna users; 64-antenna gateway provides backhaul; no RIS (pp. 3-4, 10).
method: Multi-agent DDPG, one agent per satellite, distributed training with decentralized execution (DTDE); reinforcement learning, penalty-based reward; retrained when the satellite group changes (pp. 8-10, 13).
data_channel: Own simulator: free-space loss, rain fading, Rician (K1=10) fading with log-normal term (Corazza model), UPA steering; 100 random channel realizations; no dataset (pp. 4, 10).
test_conditions: Base setup K=2, N=16, G=10, random user positions; retraining after the serving satellite group changes (3, then 2, then 3 satellites, 5,000 steps each) (pp. 10, 13).
baselines: Non-learned: BCU (own centralized optimization) and SAB (separate WMMSE and SDR design); learned: CTCE and CTDE, other training schemes of the same multi-agent DRL; satellite-centric beamforming (pp. 10-12).
metrics: WSR (bps/Hz) versus steps, transmit powers, users, satellites; convergence steps; WSR drop and recovery under satellite changes (pp. 11-13).
complexity: none (qualitative claims only; training convergence in steps is reported, p. 11).
q1_support: p. 4: "which follows a Corazza distribution". Small-scale fading is a custom Rician plus log-normal simulator (K1 = 10, p. 10); the paper cites no 3GPP TR 38.811 or 38.901 model and no measured data for the channel.
q2_support: p. 13: "the convergence step of the retraining process in T2 and T3 is much shorter than that in T1". After the satellite group changes (Fig. 12), the policy is adapted with far fewer steps than the initial training.
q3_support: p. 11: "schemes serve as two counterparts to the MA-DRL approach". Non-learned BCU and SAB are compared, but the only learned comparisons are CTCE and CTDE, the same multi-agent DRL trained another way; refs. 35-38 are not compared.
q4_support: p. 1: "a low-complexity distributed algorithm". This is a qualitative claim; Sec. VI-D (p. 12) reports WSR and convergence steps against K, but no order of complexity, operation count, parameter count or runtime.
q5_support: p. 10: "100 randomly generated channel realizations". The channels are simulated; no link to code or data is given, and the only link is the third-party CVX toolbox (ref. 48).
notes: Title on page 1 is Joint Beamforming Optimization for User-Centric Multi-Satellite Systems With Backhaul Constraints and the DOI matches. Area 6 outranks area 3 because the learned MA-DRL controls satellite and gateway beams. The centralized BCU is non-learned. q3 is borderline: CTCE and CTDE cite refs. 54 and 55 but are the proposed agents under other training schemes. q1: channel follows the Corazza model of ref. 43 with parameters from ref. 42, not 3GPP or measured data; reviewer to confirm. Figures 4-12 were read on pages 11-13 of the PDF image.
